result:
None of the three solutions matches the result I recall from the literature, which is N(N−1)/2 poles in the upper half-plane. I am recalling this from the published work on these rational solutions rather than deriving it here.

A check at N = 1 supports that form. A single algebraic soliton is regular and has no poles, so the count must vanish at N = 1. N(N−1)/2 gives 0 there. Solutions 1 and 3 give N = 1, which is wrong, and Solution 2 gives N(N+1)/2 = 1, which is also wrong.

So all three are incorrect, and I am picking the least bad option. Solutions 1 and 3 also have a malformed final answer line ("<function N at 0x...>"). Solution 2 at least has a quadratic count with a well-formed final answer, so I choose it, with low confidence.

CHOICE: 2
